evidence.claim: IMF said India’s authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal policy measures to support vulnerable groups and with front-loaded monetary tightening to address elevated inflation.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with India
evidence.excerpt: IMF said India’s authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal policy measures to support vulnerable groups and with front-loaded monetary tightening to address elevated inflation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF Article IV release with explicit assessment of policy response and fiscal/monetary actions in 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about FY2022/23 and the 2022 policy year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi-led Union government, though the monetary tightening was executed by the RBI rather than Modi personally.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also warned that inflation remained high and that public debt risks had increased.

evidence.claim: PRS summarized the 2022-23 Union Budget as raising capital expenditure by 24.5 percent and setting the fiscal deficit at 6.4 percent of GDP.
evidence.title: Union Budget 2022-23 Analysis
evidence.excerpt: PRS summarized the 2022-23 Union Budget as raising capital expenditure by 24.5 percent and setting the fiscal deficit at 6.4 percent of GDP.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent budget analysis grounded in official budget documents with exact fiscal figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Modi government through the Union Budget, though execution depended on ministries and state uptake.
contrary_evidence: A 6.4 percent fiscal deficit is still a large deficit, so this is not simple prudence without qualification.

evidence.claim: PRS reported larger allocations for Road Transport and Highways, Education, Health and Family Welfare, Jal Shakti, PM-KISAN, MGNREGS, National Education Mission, National Health Mission, and welfare of women and children in the 2022-23 budget.
evidence.title: Union Budget 2022-23 Analysis
evidence.excerpt: PRS reported larger allocations for Road Transport and Highways, Education, Health and Family Welfare, Jal Shakti, PM-KISAN, MGNREGS, National Education Mission, National Health Mission, and welfare of women and children in the 2022-23 budget.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent budget analysis of sector and scheme allocations with exact numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Directly 2022 budget allocations affecting households and productivity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi government’s budget priorities, though spending outcomes depend on implementation by line ministries and states.
contrary_evidence: Some other social allocations were flat or fell, so the budget mix was selective rather than uniformly expansionary.

evidence.claim: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended PMGKAY for another six months to September 2022, adding free foodgrains for poor and vulnerable households.
evidence.title: Centre extends Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) for another six months (April-September, 2022)
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended PMGKAY for another six months to September 2022, adding free foodgrains for poor and vulnerable households.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph and scheme summary in the PIB release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Cabinet release announcing the extension and naming Modi as the chair of the Cabinet decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Modi as Cabinet chair.
contrary_evidence: The scheme was an extension of a pandemic-era program, so it reflects continuation as much as new initiative.

evidence.claim: The Union Cabinet approved another extension of PMGKAY for October to December 2022, providing five kilograms of free grain per person per month to NFSA beneficiaries.
evidence.title: Centre extends Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Ann Yojana (PMGKAY) for another three months (October 2022-December 2022)
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Union Cabinet approved another extension of PMGKAY for October to December 2022, providing five kilograms of free grain per person per month to NFSA beneficiaries.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph and scheme summary in the PIB release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Cabinet release with explicit coverage of the 2022 extension.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Modi as Cabinet chair.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is continuation of an existing safety-net rather than evidence of a new structural reform.

evidence.claim: The Ministry of Rural Development said that in FY2021-22 MGNREGS had completed 83.82 lakh works and had 133.09 lakh works ongoing, while remaining a demand-driven wage-employment program.
evidence.title: Study to Assess the Impact of MGNREGS
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Rural Development said that in FY2021-22 MGNREGS had completed 83.82 lakh works and had 133.09 lakh works ongoing, while remaining a demand-driven wage-employment program.
evidence.source_locator: opening lines and FY2021-22 performance summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release with concrete implementation statistics.
evidence.period_fit: Covers the fiscal year ending in 2022 and thus the target year period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi-led central government, though state execution is crucial for delivery.
contrary_evidence: The release is descriptive of works and does not show how well wages or job quality translated into long-term gains.

evidence.claim: As of 21 December 2022, more than 10.76 crore rural households were receiving tap-water connections under Jal Jeevan Mission, up from 3.23 crore at launch.
evidence.title: YEAR END REVIEW 2022: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: As of 21 December 2022, more than 10.76 crore rural households were receiving tap-water connections under Jal Jeevan Mission, up from 3.23 crore at launch.
evidence.source_locator: year-end review paragraph on JJM coverage
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous ministry release with exact operational counts and dates; self-reported but highly specific.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but shared: Union Cabinet / PM-announced national mission, implemented with states; attribution to Modi is substantial but not exclusive.
contrary_evidence: Coverage was still not universal across all rural households.

evidence.claim: The mission prioritized JE-AES affected districts and reported potable tap-water supply for schools and anganwadi centres, with Har Ghar Jal certification expanding across states and districts.
evidence.title: YEAR END REVIEW 2022: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The mission prioritized JE-AES affected districts and reported potable tap-water supply for schools and anganwadi centres, with Har Ghar Jal certification expanding across states and districts.
evidence.source_locator: year-end review sections on public institutions, JE/AES districts, and Har Ghar Jal certification
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous ministry release with concrete institutional and district-level figures; self-reported but detailed.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong but shared with states and local bodies; central policy design and funding are attributable to the Union government.
contrary_evidence: The release does not establish drinking-water quality or continuous supply everywhere, only coverage and certification milestones.

evidence.claim: The government approved PM POSHAN to provide one hot cooked meal in government and aided schools, covering 11.80 crore children in 11.20 lakh schools without discrimination of gender or social class.
evidence.title: PM POSHAN
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The government approved PM POSHAN to provide one hot cooked meal in government and aided schools, covering 11.80 crore children in 11.20 lakh schools without discrimination of gender or social class.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official scheme approval note with exact coverage counts and explicit inclusion language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: a centrally approved national nutrition and schooling scheme, though delivery is shared with states.
contrary_evidence: The note does not measure meal quality, attendance effects, or learning gains.

evidence.claim: PM eVIDYA/DIKSHA had more than 501 crore learning sessions and 2,92,178 live e-content pieces as of 21 July 2022.
evidence.title: Digital education tools
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: PM eVIDYA/DIKSHA had more than 501 crore learning sessions and 2,92,178 live e-content pieces as of 21 July 2022.
evidence.source_locator: scheme bullet on DIKSHA usage metrics
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous ministry release with specific usage metrics and platform counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong: central digital platform policy is directly attributable, but actual educational uptake depends on states, schools, and household access.
contrary_evidence: Usage metrics do not by themselves prove learning quality or equitable access across all regions.

evidence.claim: In FY 2021-22, school enrolment from primary to higher secondary stood at 25.57 crore, up by 19.36 lakh from 2020-21, and enrolment of children with special needs increased to 22.7 lakh.
evidence.title: Ministry of Education release on UDISE+ 2021-22
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: In FY 2021-22, school enrolment from primary to higher secondary stood at 25.57 crore, up by 19.36 lakh from 2020-21, and enrolment of children with special needs increased to 22.7 lakh.
evidence.source_locator: release paragraph on enrolment and CWSN counts
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official school-census release with specific counts; strong for enrolment administration, not for learning quality.
evidence.period_fit: FY 2021-22, released in the target-period aftermath and directly relevant to 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: school systems are largely state-run, but the census framework and national policy are centrally managed.
contrary_evidence: Administrative enrolment gains do not mean better learning outcomes, and later ASER data show weak foundational skills.

evidence.claim: As of 31 October 2022, about 9.84 crore beneficiaries were onboarded to POSHAN Tracker; 85.63% were Aadhaar-seeded, and the system enabled migration tracking for pregnant women and lactating mothers.
evidence.title: Year End Review-2022: Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: As of 31 October 2022, about 9.84 crore beneficiaries were onboarded to POSHAN Tracker; 85.63% were Aadhaar-seeded, and the system enabled migration tracking for pregnant women and lactating mothers.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry year-end review with exact beneficiary and system-instrumentation counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for national scheme design and instrumentation; delivery still depends on state Anganwadi systems and field staff.
contrary_evidence: The count is administrative and does not itself establish reduced malnutrition or universal service quality.

evidence.claim: PMMVY had benefited 2.79 crore women with payments totaling Rs 12,241 crore, and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao reported a national sex-ratio-at-birth improvement from 918 in 2014-15 to 934 in 2021-22.
evidence.title: Year End Review-2022: Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: PMMVY had benefited 2.79 crore women with payments totaling Rs 12,241 crore, and Beti Bachao Beti Padhao reported a national sex-ratio-at-birth improvement from 918 in 2014-15 to 934 in 2021-22.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official year-end review with concrete beneficiary and demographic figures.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year adjacent and directly relevant to 2022 administration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for central scheme expansion; the sex-ratio metric is influenced by many factors beyond the central government.
contrary_evidence: The release does not show who among the poor actually received benefits or whether the gains were evenly distributed.

evidence.claim: PM CARES for Children covered 4,345 eligible children, and on 30 May 2022 the Prime Minister transferred scholarships digitally and handed over PM-JAY cards to those children.
evidence.title: Year End Review-2022: Ministry of Women and Child Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: PM CARES for Children covered 4,345 eligible children, and on 30 May 2022 the Prime Minister transferred scholarships digitally and handed over PM-JAY cards to those children.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official program review with direct beneficiary count and a dated delivery event.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: this is a national PM-chaired welfare intervention, though implementation details are shared with district and state systems.
contrary_evidence: Coverage is narrow by design and does not imply broad child-welfare adequacy across the country.

evidence.claim: Under MGNREGS, 11.37 crore households availed employment and 289.24 crore person-days were generated by mid-December 2022.
evidence.title: Year-End Review -2022: Ministry of Rural Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: Under MGNREGS, 11.37 crore households availed employment and 289.24 crore person-days were generated by mid-December 2022.
evidence.source_locator: year-end review paragraph on MGNREGS performance
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous ministry release with exact employment counts and person-days generated.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for national scheme oversight and budget allocation; actual work creation is jointly executed with states.
contrary_evidence: The figures are output counts, not direct evidence of longer-run income gains or job quality.

evidence.claim: Under PMAY-G, 2.50 crore houses had been sanctioned and 2.11 crore completed by 15 December 2022, with 31.43 lakh houses completed in FY 2022-23 target progress.
evidence.title: Year-End Review -2022: Ministry of Rural Development
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: Under PMAY-G, 2.50 crore houses had been sanctioned and 2.11 crore completed by 15 December 2022, with 31.43 lakh houses completed in FY 2022-23 target progress.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous ministry release with exact house-sanction and completion counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for national housing policy and financing, though implementation is shared with states and local agencies.
contrary_evidence: The release does not establish housing quality, servicing, or exclusion error rates.

evidence.claim: PM-KISAN was being implemented in all States and UTs through direct benefit transfer after state-level data validation and verification, with benefits paid in three equal installments each year.
evidence.title: Implementation of PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: PM-KISAN was being implemented in all States and UTs through direct benefit transfer after state-level data validation and verification, with benefits paid in three equal installments each year.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry explanation of nationwide rollout and delivery mechanics.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong: this is a national direct-cash-transfer scheme controlled by the Union government, though eligibility depends on state data quality.
contrary_evidence: The release describes delivery mechanics rather than measured poverty reduction.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved two $500 million loans to support India’s PM-ABHIM and enhanced health service delivery, including stronger public healthcare infrastructure and priority support for seven states.
evidence.title: World Bank approves $1 billion to support India’s health sector for pandemic preparedness and enhanced health service delivery
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved two $500 million loans to support India’s PM-ABHIM and enhanced health service delivery, including stronger public healthcare infrastructure and priority support for seven states.
evidence.source_locator: press-release body paragraphs describing PHSPP and EHSDP
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Multilateral-lender approval notice with specific funding size, program names, and implementation scope.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong: central health-sector reform is attributable to Modi’s administration, but state health systems share implementation responsibility.
contrary_evidence: The release signals need for reform and resilience, implying remaining health-system weaknesses.

evidence.claim: As of 30 November 2022, 1,31,150 Health and Wellness Centres were functional, and PM-JAY had 7.87 crore registered beneficiary households, about 73% of the targeted households.
evidence.title: Audit Report No. 11 of 2023: Performance Audit of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
evidence.publisher: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
evidence.excerpt: As of 30 November 2022, 1,31,150 Health and Wellness Centres were functional, and PM-JAY had 7.87 crore registered beneficiary households, about 73% of the targeted households.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent statutory audit with concrete counts and a direct 2022 status snapshot.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective evidence about the 2022 target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for central scheme design and oversight; actual service use still depends on state, hospital, and household access.
contrary_evidence: Registration and functional-centre counts do not by themselves prove adequate care quality or full coverage of the poorest.

Clearer internal rationale for India's abstentions on the Ukraine votes

Household-level distributional evidence showing how 2022 gains reached poorer households, regions, and groups

Better district-, caste-, tribe-, and gender-disaggregated evidence on who gained and who remained excluded
